title: 2019 Baulkham Hills Legal Studies Trial
notes: No multiple-choice answer key was found in the paper; no shared stimulus groups or figures appeared in Section I.

questions.stem: What is the legal term for the physical act of committing a crime?
questions.answerNote: Actus reus is the physical element of an offence.

questions.stem: What is the role of a victim’s impact statement?

options.A: It gives the victim a say in charge bargaining
options.B: It allows the victim to have a say in the sentencing process
options.C: It allows the victim to present written evidence in the determination of guilt
options.D: It allows the victim a say in the determination of evidence

questions.answerNote: A victim impact statement informs sentencing about the offence’s impact on the victim.

questions.stem: Who has the burden of proof in the Children’s Court?
questions.answerNote: The prosecution bears the burden of proving the charge.

questions.stem: Greg is stopped by the police for a random breath test. What must he do?

options.A: He must submit to the breath test
options.B: He does not have to do anything
options.C: He must answer all questions asked by the police
options.D: He must get out of the car

questions.answerNote: Drivers are legally required to submit to a random breath test when lawfully requested.

questions.stem: Ellen is arrested and charged as part of an international drug smuggling ring. What type of crime is this an example of?
questions.answerNote: Drug smuggling across national borders is transnational crime.

questions.stem: Selling alcohol to people under the age of 18 is an example of which type of crime?
questions.answerNote: Selling alcohol to minors is a regulatory offence commonly taught as strict liability (C); A (public order offence) is a weaker second option.

questions.stem: What is the main consideration in determining parole?
questions.answerNote: Parole authorities primarily assess the risk to community safety.

questions.stem: Which feature distinguishes a summary offence from an indictable offence?

options.B: The court which will hear an appeal
options.D: Whether it is a white collar crime

questions.answerNote: Summary offences are generally less serious than indictable offences.

questions.stem: During the criminal investigation process, young offenders are classified as ‘vulnerable people’. What does this mean?

options.A: They can’t be arrested for a serious offence
options.B: They can’t be searched after being arrested
options.C: They can’t be fingerprinted after being arrested
options.D: They can’t be questioned without a support person

questions.answerNote: A young suspect must have a support person present during police questioning.

questions.stem: How is the truth of the evidence, tested in an adversarial trial?
questions.answerNote: Cross-examination tests the reliability and credibility of evidence.

questions.stem: What is the role of the Public Defender?

options.A: To represent public officials charged with criminal offences
options.B: To represent victims of crime who have legal aid
options.C: To represent police officers in the court of law
options.D: To represent people charged with serious indictable offences who have legal aid

questions.answerNote: Public Defenders represent eligible accused people in serious criminal matters.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a civil and political right?

options.C: The right to an adequate standard of living

questions.answerNote: The right to life is a civil and political right; The others are economic, social and cultural rights.

questions.stem: The minority Muslim group of a particular country are placed in concentration camps for ‘re-education purposes’. Which human right is being denied?

options.C: The right to freedom of religion

questions.answerNote: The targeting of a Muslim minority for religious identity violates freedom of religion.

questions.stem: Which of the following defences can lead to an acquittal?
questions.answerNote: Self-defence, if established, is a complete defence and results in acquittal.

questions.stem: Which of the following has the power to prosecute human rights offenders?
questions.answerNote: The ICC prosecutes individuals for core international crimes, including crimes against humanity and genocide.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a true statement about the Declaration of Human Rights?

options.A: It is binding and enforceable on all states under international law
options.B: It is mostly ignored by states
options.C: It is generally accepted statements that have become part of international customary law
options.D: It is ratified by all nations

questions.answerNote: The Universal Declaration itself is not a binding treaty, though many of its principles are customary law.

questions.stem: JD has been charged with armed robbery and is awaiting his trial. Which of the following would be a reason that JD is held in remand?

options.A: He is deemed an unacceptable risk to the community

questions.answerNote: A court may refuse bail and remand an accused considered an unacceptable community risk.

questions.stem: The fact that human rights cannot be taken away from anyone is an example of which characteristic?
questions.answerNote: Inalienable rights cannot be surrendered or taken away.

questions.stem: Sam, who is 30, is charged with stealing from a department store. He has a number of prior convictions. The judge said he has good prospects of rehabilitation. What penalty is he most likely to receive?
questions.answerNote: Prior convictions make a non-conviction order unlikely and a good rehabilitation prospect points to a community-based sentence such as an Intensive Correction Order (B); Imprisonment (A) is the other plausible answer.

questions.stem: Harry is convicted of murder and appeals to the NSW Court of Criminal Appeal. What outcome will lead to an acquittal of the charges and release from prison?

options.B: An order for a retrial before a different judge

questions.answerNote: Quashing the conviction sets it aside and allows release if no other basis for detention exists.
